q: A member of the Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament holds office as a member of that Committee for a term of:

options.A: Five years
options.B: Three years
options.C: The remaining term of the Lok Sabha
options.D: One year

q: A probationer asks how the corpus of the Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF), set up in 2001-02, was built up. The corpus was made up of:

options.A: The safety surcharge on passenger fares alone
options.B: Market borrowings raised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation alone
options.C: A contribution from the General Revenues (Ministry of Finance) together with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares
options.D: Appropriations made from the Railway Pension Fund

q: The first batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants in a financial year is ordinarily presented in the Monsoon Session. The second batch of Supplementary Demands during the year is ordinarily presented to Parliament in the:

options.A: Budget Session
options.B: Winter Session
options.C: Monsoon Session
options.D: A special session convened for the purpose

q: In the terminology of railway accounts, the expression 'Debt Heads' is used collectively for:

options.A: The revenue heads of account only
options.B: The capital heads of account only
options.C: The debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads of account
options.D: The earnings heads of account

q: A zonal railway proposes to meet the cost of constructing an entirely new railway line out of the Depreciation Reserve Fund. Which of the following is NOT a permissible use of the Depreciation Reserve Fund?

options.A: Renewal and replacement of track
options.B: Construction of a new railway line
options.C: Renewal and replacement of bridges
options.D: Renewal and replacement of rolling stock

q: After examining the Appropriation Accounts and the audit reports thereon, the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament presents its reports to:

options.A: The Rajya Sabha only
options.B: The President of India
options.C: The Lok Sabha
options.D: The Finance Minister

q: The divisions and field units of a zonal railway prepare their budget estimates and forward them for submission to the Railway Board. Before such submission, these estimates are:

options.A: Sent directly by each division to the Railway Board
options.B: Consolidated and scrutinised at the headquarters of the zonal railway
options.C: Audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Approved by the Ministry of Finance

q: At the zonal level, the distribution of the budget allotment among the divisions and units of a zonal railway is made with reference to the units of appropriation, namely:

options.A: Sub-Major Heads for revenue expenditure and Plan Heads for capital (works) expenditure
options.B: Primary Units for both revenue and capital expenditure
options.C: Plan Heads for revenue expenditure and Sub-Major Heads for capital expenditure
options.D: Detailed Heads for both revenue and capital expenditure

q: In the books of a zonal railway, the suspense head 'PAO Suspense' shows a debit balance at the close of a month. This debit balance represents:

options.A: Amounts paid or adjusted by the Railways on behalf of other Ministries/Departments, pending settlement or recovery from the Pay and Accounts Office concerned
options.B: Amounts received on behalf of other Ministries, pending payment to them
options.C: The cash balance of the Railways held with the Reserve Bank
options.D: Cheques issued by the Railways but not yet paid by the bank

q: In the books of a zonal railway, the suspense head 'AG Suspense' shows a credit balance at the close of a month. This credit balance represents:

options.A: Amounts paid on behalf of State Governments, pending recovery
options.B: Amounts received or collected by the Railways for State Governments/Accountants General, pending remittance or adjustment
options.C: Loans raised by the Railways from the market
options.D: Wages drawn but remaining unpaid at the end of the month

q: In the books of a zonal railway, the suspense head 'PSB Suspense' shows a debit balance. This debit balance represents:

options.A: Cheques deposited with the bank but not yet realised
options.B: Amounts credited by the bank to the Railways' account, pending advice
options.C: Payments made by the accredited public sector bank on behalf of the Railways, pending receipt of the bank's advice and adjustment to the final heads
options.D: Amounts due from stations on account of traffic transactions

q: In the books of a zonal railway, the suspense head 'Traffic Suspense' shows a credit balance. This credit balance represents:

options.A: Debits raised against stations, pending recovery
options.B: Traffic amounts and earnings held pending apportionment or adjustment in favour of the stations or other railways concerned
options.C: The value of stores held in stock in depots
options.D: Advances made to contractors, pending adjustment

q: Cheques and bills received by a zonal railway have been deposited with the bank and stand debited under the head 'Cheques and Bills'. The debit side of the head is cleared when:

options.A: A cheque is issued by the Cash & Pay Office
options.B: A bill is passed for payment by the Accounts Office
options.C: The bank intimates the realisation, or credit, of the cheques and bills deposited with it
options.D: The payee presents the cheque at his own bank

q: At the level of the Government of India, the watch over the cash position of the Government with the Reserve Bank of India, as an instrument of exchequer control over expenditure, is kept by:

options.A: The Railway Board
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Ministry of Finance, keeping watch over the cash position of the Government with the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: The Estimates Committee of Parliament

q: The Cash Office of a zonal railway receives the earnings remitted by the stations of the railway. On receipt, the Cash Office checks these remittances with reference to:

options.A: The Cash Remittance Notes accompanying the remittances
options.B: The Station Balance Sheets rendered to the Traffic Accounts Office
options.C: The Transfer Certificates received from other railways
options.D: The Pink Book of the railway

q: In the earlier practice, zonal railways rendered an Approximate Account Current in addition to the final monthly account. The Approximate Account Current served mainly to:

options.A: Replace the final monthly account altogether
options.B: Furnish the Railway Board with approximate figures of the month's transactions in advance, pending the final compilation of the account
options.C: Report only the balances under the suspense heads
options.D: Obtain the supplementary grant for the month

q: Materials are released from a work of renewal and replacement of an asset on a zonal railway and are taken back into use or stock. Such released materials are accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting their value to Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: Ignoring them in the accounts of the work
options.C: Debiting their value to Capital as a fresh asset
options.D: Crediting their value to the renewal work concerned, thereby reducing the charge to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

q: A workshop of one zonal railway carries out repairs on the rolling stock belonging to another zonal railway. The cost of these repairs is adjusted between the two railways:

options.A: By daily remittance of cash by the debtor railway
options.B: Out of the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Through transfer transactions, without any movement of cash between the railways
options.D: Through the Traffic Suspense account only

q: Licence fees are realised by a zonal railway from the catering units and book stalls operating at its stations. In the railway accounts, these licence fees are classified under:

options.A: Passenger earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Other Coaching Earnings
options.D: Sundry Other Earnings

q: For a particular period, the earnings apportioned to a zonal railway after apportionment of through-traffic earnings exceed the earnings originated and collected by that railway. The net result of apportionment for that railway is:

options.A: A net credit due to that railway, adjusted through transfer transactions with the other railways concerned
options.B: A net debit against that railway, adjusted through transfer transactions
options.C: Nil, the excess lapsing to the Railway Board
options.D: A credit to the Development Fund of that railway

q: The Trial Balance extracted from the General Books of a zonal railway does not agree, and the difference cannot be located immediately, though the accounts have to be closed. Pending the location and rectification of the error, the difference is:

options.A: Written off to the working expenses of the year
options.B: Carried to the Balance Sheet as a permanent asset of the Railways
options.C: Placed to a Suspense Account, so that the Trial Balance is made to agree, and cleared when the error is located and rectified
options.D: Adjusted against the balance under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank'

q: In the Budget section of a zonal railway, a probationer is asked to locate the one Budget document that specifically reports the progress made in implementing the announcements made in the Budget of the previous year. That document is the:

options.A: Expenditure Profile
options.B: Outcome Budget
options.C: Key to Budget Documents
options.D: Document on the Implementation of Budget Announcements

q: At a study circle on the sharing of Union revenues, two Articles of the Constitution are taken up together. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the duties referred to in Article 268 of the Constitution from the taxes referred to in Article 269?

options.A: The duties under Article 268 are levied and collected by the States themselves, whereas the taxes under Article 269 are shared between the Union and the States
options.B: The duties under Article 268 are levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States, whereas the taxes under Article 269 are levied and collected by the Union but assigned wholly to the States, their proceeds not forming part of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Both the duties under Article 268 and the taxes under Article 269 are levied, collected and retained by the Union alone
options.D: The duties under Article 268 are assigned to the States by the Finance Commission, whereas the taxes under Article 269 are levied by the States and collected by the Union

q: For sharing a Union tax between the Union and the States, its gross proceeds have first to be reduced by the cost of collection to arrive at the net proceeds. The amount of such net proceeds in a year is finally determined on the basis of:

options.A: The figures worked out by the Budget Division of the Ministry of Finance
options.B: The recommendations of the Finance Commission for that year
options.C: The calculation and certificate of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whose certificate is final
options.D: The report of the Public Accounts Committee on the Finance Accounts

q: A State Finance Commission has reviewed the finances of the Panchayats and Municipalities of a State. On the basis of its recommendations, the measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of the State in order to supplement the resources of those bodies are recommended to the President by:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: The State Finance Commission itself, directly to the President
options.C: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj
options.D: The Finance Commission constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution

q: A zonal railway receives two kinds of amendments affecting the heads of account it uses, one touching the Government List and the other the railway classification in the Finance Code. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the authority for amending the classification of accounts?

options.A: Amendments to the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account are issued by the Controller General of Accounts, whereas amendments and corrections to the railway classification of accounts contained in the Finance Code are issued by the Railway Board through Correction Slips
options.B: Both the Government List and the railway classification are amended by the Railway Board
options.C: Amendments to the Government List are issued by the Railway Board, whereas the railway classification is amended by the Controller General of Accounts
options.D: Both the lists are amended by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

q:
Consider the following statements about the Estimates Committee of Parliament:
1. The Estimates Committee takes up for examination the estimates of only such Ministries, departments or subjects as it selects each year, and not the estimates of all the Ministries in a single year.
2. The Estimates Committee itself votes the Demands for Grants after examining them, whereafter the Lok Sabha passes them without further discussion.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
At an accounts review meeting, two propositions about the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways are examined. Consider the following statements in this connection:
1. In the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways, the actual expenditure is compared separately with the grants voted by Parliament and with the appropriations for expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. A saving available under the charged portion of a grant can be utilised, by re-appropriation, to meet an excess under the voted portion of the same grant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A newly posted Accounts Assistant confuses the statement of estimates laid before Parliament at the start of the year with the annual account of the Railways compiled after its close. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Annual Financial Statement from the Finance Accounts of the Railways?

options.A: The Annual Financial Statement is the statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the year, laid before both Houses of Parliament, whereas the Finance Accounts present the actual receipts and disbursements of the completed year, classified under the Major Heads of account
options.B: The Annual Financial Statement presents the actual accounts of the completed year, whereas the Finance Accounts present the estimates for the ensuing year
options.C: Both the Annual Financial Statement and the Finance Accounts are voted by the Lok Sabha
options.D: The Annual Financial Statement is compiled by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas the Finance Accounts are presented by the Finance Minister

q: Two compilations of the Accounts Office are sometimes confused with each other — one summarising the month's transactions head-wise and the other exhibiting the balances under the debt heads. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Classified Abstract from the Debt Head Report of a railway?

options.A: The Classified Abstract is the head-wise summary of the month's transactions, compiled from the subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted, whereas the Debt Head Report exhibits the balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads as recorded in the General Books
options.B: The Classified Abstract exhibits the balances under the debt heads, whereas the Debt Head Report summarises the month's transactions for posting the General Books
options.C: Both the documents are rendered by the stations to the Traffic Accounts Office
options.D: The Classified Abstract is prepared by the Audit Department, whereas the Debt Head Report is prepared by the executive departments

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Suspense Register from the Debt Head Report of a railway?

options.A: The Suspense Register shows the balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads, whereas the Debt Head Report watches the clearance of individual outstanding items
options.B: The Suspense Register is maintained to watch the outstanding items under each suspense head and secure their clearance, whereas the Debt Head Report is a monthly statement showing the balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads
options.C: Both the Suspense Register and the Debt Head Report are monthly statements rendered to the Railway Board along with the Account Current
options.D: The Suspense Register is rendered to the Railway Board every month, whereas the Debt Head Report is maintained in the Accounts Office only

q:
Two propositions about the preparation of the annual accounts of the Railways are put to a probationer for his comments. Consider the following statements in this connection:
1. The Appropriation Accounts of the Railways are prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
2. The Appropriation Accounts and the Finance Accounts of the Railways are prepared from the accounts of the financial year after their closure.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The annual appropriations to two Railway Funds are assessed on entirely different bases, one linked to the assets of the Railways and the other to their pension liability. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the basis on which appropriations are made to the Depreciation Reserve Fund from the basis of appropriation to the Railway Pension Fund?

options.A: Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is assessed on actuarial valuation, whereas appropriation to the Pension Fund is assessed on the original cost and codal life of assets
options.B: Both appropriations are assessed with reference to the original cost and codal life of the assets concerned
options.C: Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is assessed with reference to the original cost of the assets and their prescribed (codal) life, whereas the appropriation to the Pension Fund is assessed with reference to the actuarial valuation of the pension liability
options.D: Appropriation to the Pension Fund is assessed with reference to the original cost and codal life of assets, whereas appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is assessed on actuarial valuation

q: Two publications connected with the Union Budget are sometimes confused with each other — one reviewing the state of the economy and the other summarising the Budget figures. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Economic Survey from the Budget document 'Budget at a Glance'?

options.A: Both the documents present the detailed Demands for Grants of the Ministries
options.B: The Economic Survey presents a summary of the Budget figures, whereas 'Budget at a Glance' reviews the state of the economy
options.C: The Economic Survey reviews the state of the economy and is presented shortly before the presentation of the Union Budget, whereas 'Budget at a Glance' presents a brief summary of the Budget, showing the receipts, the expenditure and the various deficit indicators in a nutshell
options.D: The Economic Survey is presented by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas 'Budget at a Glance' is presented by the Reserve Bank of India

q: An audit party on a zonal railway conducts two kinds of audit on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, one verifying the availability and application of grants and the other testing expenditure against the canons of financial propriety. Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'appropriation audit' from 'propriety audit'?

options.A: Both the audits are concerned only with the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts
options.B: Appropriation audit examines expenditure against the canons of financial propriety, whereas propriety audit verifies the availability of grants
options.C: Appropriation audit is conducted by the Accounts Department as an internal check, whereas propriety audit is conducted by the Public Accounts Committee
options.D: Appropriation audit verifies that the moneys shown in the accounts as having been disbursed were legally available for, and were applied to, the services and purposes for which the grants and appropriations were made by Parliament, whereas propriety audit examines expenditure against the canons of financial propriety, bringing out cases of wasteful, infructuous or avoidable expenditure

q: In the financing of the Railway Plan, two kinds of resources are sometimes confused with each other — one raised from the market and the other generated by the Railways themselves. Which of the following correctly distinguishes Extra Budgetary Resources from the internal resources of the Railways?

options.A: Both the resources are generated from the surplus of the Railways and carried in their fund balances
options.B: Extra Budgetary Resources are generated from the revenues of the Railways, whereas the internal resources are borrowed from the market
options.C: Extra Budgetary Resources are voted by Parliament as part of the Demands for Grants, whereas the internal resources require no budgetary provision at all
options.D: Extra Budgetary Resources are raised from the market, as through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation, and their servicing is the responsibility of the Railways, whereas the internal resources are generated by the Railways themselves from their revenues and fund balances and are used to finance a part of the plan outlay

q: A probationer is asked to explain how the first record of a transaction in a railway differs from its record in the principal book of account. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the books of original entry of a railway from its Ledger?

options.A: Both the books record the transactions finally, head-wise, in the form of accounts
options.B: The books of original entry are the General Books of the railway, whereas the Ledger is a subsidiary book of first record
options.C: The Ledger is maintained only in the executive offices, whereas the books of original entry are maintained only by the Audit Department
options.D: The books of original entry, that is, the subsidiary books such as the Cash Book and the Journal Book, are those in which the transactions are first recorded in detail, whereas the Ledger is the principal book of account in which an account is kept for every head of account and from which the Trial Balance is extracted

q: Two financial advisers of the Railways, one at the zonal level and the other at the Railway Board level, are sometimes confused with each other. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway from the Financial Commissioner (Railways)?

options.A: Both the officers function as the financial adviser to the General Manager of a zonal railway
options.B: The head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway is a Member of the Railway Board, whereas the Financial Commissioner heads the accounts organisation of one zonal railway
options.C: The head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway is appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas the Financial Commissioner is elected by the Railway Board
options.D: The head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway, the Principal Financial Adviser, heads the accounts organisation of the railway and functions as the financial adviser to its General Manager, whereas the Financial Commissioner (Railways) is a Member of the Railway Board and its principal financial adviser on matters of railway finance

q: Two documents connected with the remittance and receipt of station earnings are sometimes confused with each other — one accompanying the cash remitted by a station and the other rendered daily by the bank. Which of the following correctly distinguishes a Cash Remittance Note from the bank scroll in railway accounts?

options.A: Both the documents are daily statements rendered by the accredited bank to the Accounts Office
options.B: A Cash Remittance Note is rendered by the bank to the station, whereas the bank scroll accompanies the cash remitted by a station
options.C: A Cash Remittance Note is a register maintained in the Traffic Accounts Office, whereas the bank scroll is a register maintained at the station
options.D: A Cash Remittance Note is the document which accompanies the earnings remitted by a station to the Cash Office or the bank, whereas the bank scroll is the daily statement of receipts and payments rendered by the accredited bank to the Accounts Office, from which the bank's transactions are reconciled with the railway books

q: The lease charges paid by the Railways to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation have two components which are treated very differently in the accounts. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the capital component from the interest component of these lease charges?

options.A: Both the components are charged to revenue as part of the working expenses of the Railways
options.B: The capital component is recovered from the Depreciation Reserve Fund, whereas the interest component is charged to Capital
options.C: The capital component is treated as a deposit with the Corporation, whereas the interest component is treated as a loan to it
options.D: The capital component is accounted for as capital outlay under the Plan Head for Leased Assets, whereas the interest component, being a finance charge, is charged to revenue as part of the working expenses of the Railways

q: A zonal railway proposes an operational improvement work which is necessary for efficient working but is not expected to be directly remunerative. Such unremunerative operational improvement works are financed from:

options.A: Capital
options.B: DF-III of the Development Fund
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: The Capital Fund

q: In the books of a zonal railway, a debit balance has accumulated under the suspense head 'PAO Suspense'. Such a debit balance represents:

options.A: Amounts received on behalf of other Ministries, pending payment to them
options.B: The cash balance of the Railways held with the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Amounts paid or adjusted by the Railways on behalf of other Ministries/Departments, pending settlement or recovery from the Pay and Accounts Office concerned
options.D: Cheques issued by the Railways but not yet paid by the bank

q: A transfer transaction between two railways involves no actual movement of cash and is a mere book adjustment without financial effect. Such a transaction is intimated to the respondent railway through:

options.A: A TWFA advice
options.B: A Cash Remittance Note
options.C: An Advice of Internal Check
options.D: A Money Receipt

q: While finalising the papers to accompany the Appropriation Accounts of his railway, an Accounts Officer is required to attach, as an annexure to those Accounts, the:

options.A: The Trial Balance
options.B: The Pink Book statement of works
options.C: The Suspense Register
options.D: The Stock Adjustment Account

q: Under E-Recon, a transfer transaction originated by one railway remains unmatched or unaccepted by the respondent railway for a considerable time. The correct treatment of such a transaction is that it:

options.A: Is written off automatically at the close of the month
options.B: Remains outstanding under the head 'Transfer Railways' and is pursued with the respondent railway till it is matched and accepted
options.C: Is converted into a cash transaction through the Reserve Bank
options.D: Is transferred to the Railway Pension Fund

q: Within the same grant, funds are to be re-appropriated between two works which fall under the same Plan Head. Such a re-appropriation can be sanctioned by:

options.A: The Railway Board only
options.B: The Divisional Railway Manager alone
options.C: The General Manager of the zonal railway, with the concurrence of the associated finance
options.D: The Principal Financial Adviser alone, without the General Manager's sanction

q: Funds are to be re-appropriated from one Sub-Major Head to another Sub-Major Head under Major Head 3002, the Sub-Major Head being the unit of appropriation for revenue expenditure. The sanction required for such a re-appropriation is that of:

options.A: The General Manager of the zonal railway
options.B: The Divisional Railway Manager
options.C: The Principal Financial Adviser of the zonal railway
options.D: The Railway Board

q: The cash position of the Government with the Reserve Bank of India is watched, and the pace of expenditure regulated at the level of the Government of India, as an exercise of exchequer control, through:

options.A: The Ministry of Finance, keeping watch over the cash position of the Government with the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Railway Board
options.D: The Estimates Committee of Parliament

q: Valuable materials are released from a work of renewal and replacement of an asset and are taken back into stock. The value of such released materials is accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting it to Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways
options.B: Crediting it to the renewal work concerned, thereby reducing the charge to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Debiting it to Capital as a fresh asset
options.D: Ignoring it in the accounts of the work

q: The corpus of the Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF), set up in 2001-02, was made up of:

options.A: The safety surcharge on passenger fares alone
options.B: Market borrowings raised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation alone
options.C: Appropriations made from the Railway Pension Fund
options.D: A contribution from the General Revenues (Ministry of Finance) together with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares

q: In the railway payment system, 'CIPS' is associated with:

options.A: Centralised electronic payment of bills and other payments across the Railways through the accredited bank
options.B: Computerised reservation of passenger accommodation
options.C: Apportionment of through-traffic earnings among railways
options.D: Electronic auction for the sale of scrap

q: Part A of the Traffic Book deals with the apportionment of Coaching earnings. Coaching earnings comprise:

options.A: Goods earnings and Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: Passenger earnings only
options.C: Passenger earnings and Other Coaching earnings
options.D: Sundry Other Earnings only

q: A debit is raised by one railway against another through a Transfer Certificate, but the respondent railway does not agree with the debit raised against it. The correct course for the respondent railway is to:

options.A: Pay the amount immediately and claim a refund later
options.B: Return the Transfer Certificate with its objections, the item remaining outstanding till the matter is settled
options.C: Write off the amount with the sanction of its General Manager
options.D: Charge the amount to its ordinary working expenses

q: In the books of a zonal railway, the remittance head 'Remittances into Banks' normally shows:

options.A: A credit balance
options.B: A nil balance at the close of every day
options.C: A balance only in the March accounts of the year
options.D: A debit balance, representing the remittances made into the bank which are awaiting credit by the bank

q: In railway accounts, the expression 'Debt Heads' is used collectively for:

options.A: The debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads of account
options.B: The revenue heads of account only
options.C: The capital heads of account only
options.D: The earnings heads of account

q: A proposal to finance one of the following purposes out of the Depreciation Reserve Fund is objected to by the Accounts Office as an impermissible use of the Fund. The purpose objected to is:

options.A: Renewal and replacement of track
options.B: Renewal and replacement of bridges
options.C: Construction of a new railway line
options.D: Renewal and replacement of rolling stock

q: The signalling equipment at a station has become over-aged and its replacement, being a safety-related renewal, is taken up on the Railways. Such a work is financed from:

options.A: The Development Fund
options.B: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.C: The Railway Pension Fund
options.D: The Debt Service Fund

q: Earnings of the PRS/UTS systems are transferred electronically by the accredited bank during the day, but the amount has not yet been credited to the Railways' account at the close of the day. In the railway accounts, such earnings are shown as:

options.A: Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: A credit balance under Traffic Suspense
options.C: Deposits with Reserve Bank
options.D: Cash-in-Transit

q: The Trial Balance extracted from the General Books of a railway does not agree, and the difference cannot be located immediately, though the accounts have to be closed. Pending the location and rectification of the error, the difference is:

options.A: Placed to a Suspense Account, so that the Trial Balance is made to agree, and cleared when the error is located and rectified
options.B: Written off to the working expenses of the year
options.C: Carried to the Balance Sheet as a permanent asset of the Railways
options.D: Adjusted against the balance under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank'

q: Along with the Budget papers, Parliament receives a document which reports the follow-up action taken on the announcements made in the Budget of the previous year. That document is the:

options.A: Expenditure Profile
options.B: Outcome Budget
options.C: Document on the Implementation of Budget Announcements
options.D: Key to Budget Documents

q: An audit party verifies, from the accounts of a railway, that every sum shown as disbursed was legally available for the service to which it was applied, and was so applied in terms of the grant or appropriation made by Parliament. This form of audit, conducted on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, is known as:

options.A: Performance audit
options.B: Appropriation audit
options.C: Propriety audit
options.D: Efficiency audit

q: In a Works Programme document of a zonal railway, a clerk comes across the abbreviation 'LAW' used in connection with the works approved for inclusion in the programme. The abbreviation stands for:

options.A: List of Approved Works
options.B: List of Anticipated Works
options.C: Ledger of All Works
options.D: List of Authorised Workshops

q: Expenditure is incurred on a work by an officer without obtaining the sanction of the authority competent to sanction that expenditure. Such expenditure is termed:

options.A: Unauthorised expenditure
options.B: Excess expenditure
options.C: Charged expenditure
options.D: Unsanctioned expenditure

q: For preparing the monthly Debt Head Report of his railway, showing the balances under the debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads, an Accounts Officer takes those balances from:

options.A: The station balance sheets rendered by the stations
options.B: The bank scrolls received from the accredited bank
options.C: The balances as recorded in the General Ledger (General Books) of the railway
options.D: The Works Registers maintained in the Accounts Office

q: Stores are issued from a stores depot to a revenue work of the railway. In the accounts, the issue is credited to:

options.A: Manufacturing Suspense
options.B: Stores Suspense
options.C: Demands Recoverable
options.D: Miscellaneous Advances

q: The declared provisions of the Finance Bill relating to certain duties take immediate effect on the introduction of the Bill in the Lok Sabha, under a statute which was enacted in the year:

Which of the following grants made by Parliament under Article 116 of the Constitution is often described as a 'blank cheque' given to the Government, because, on account of the magnitude or the indefinite character of the service, the demand cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Demand for Grant?

options.A: Vote on Account
options.B: Exceptional Grant
options.C: Token Grant
options.D: Vote of Credit

q: While distributing the budget allotment for works (capital) expenditure among the units of a zonal railway, the Accounts Office treats as the unit of appropriation the:

options.A: The Sub-Major Head
options.B: The Primary Unit
options.C: The Plan Head
options.D: The Detailed Head

q: In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the Special Railway Safety Fund was maintained in the Public Account of India under Major Head:
Postings in the Ledger of a zonal railway are made from:

options.A: The station balance sheets rendered by the stations
options.B: The closing totals of the Journal and the Classified Abstract
options.C: The bank scrolls received from the accredited bank
options.D: The Works Registers maintained in the Accounts Office

q: Supplementary Demands for Grants are ordinarily presented during a financial year in three batches. The first of these batches is ordinarily presented to Parliament in the:

options.A: Budget Session
options.B: Winter Session
options.C: Special Session
options.D: Monsoon Session

q: Of the three batches in which Supplementary Demands for Grants are ordinarily presented during a financial year, the second batch is ordinarily presented to Parliament in the:

options.A: Winter Session
options.B: Budget Session
options.C: Monsoon Session
options.D: A special session convened for the purpose

q: The Contingency Fund of India, established under Article 267 of the Constitution, is held as an imprest at the disposal of the President. The working of this Fund is regulated by the provisions of:

options.A: The General Financial Rules
options.B: The FRBM Act, 2003
options.C: The Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950
options.D: The Appropriation Act of the year concerned

q: A private member of the Lok Sabha wishes to introduce a Money Bill in the House. The correct position in the matter is that a Money Bill can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only:

options.A: By any member of the House
options.B: By a Minister, that is, it can only be a Government Bill
options.C: By the Chairman of the Estimates Committee
options.D: By a member authorised by the President

q: A question arises whether the amount granted through a Vote on Account at the beginning of the budgetary process is over and above the full grant voted for the year. The correct position in the matter is that the amount so granted:

options.A: Is in addition to the total grant voted for the year
options.B: Is expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Lapses if it is not spent within one month of the grant
options.D: Forms part of the total grant for the year and is merged in it when the full grant is voted

q: To tide over a temporary mismatch in its cash flow, the Government of India issues Cash Management Bills in the market. The maturity period of these Bills is:

options.A: Less than 91 days
options.B: Exactly 364 days
options.C: More than one year
options.D: Exactly 182 days

q: The Reserve Bank of India issues Treasury Bills on behalf of the Government of India for raising short-term funds from the market. These Bills are issued in the maturities of:

options.A: 30 days, 60 days and 90 days
options.B: One year, three years and five years
options.C: 91 days, 182 days and 364 days
options.D: 14 days and 28 days

q: One of the financial committees of Parliament examines the estimates of the Ministries with a view to suggesting economies and improvements in organisation and efficiency. That committee, the Estimates Committee, consists of:

options.A: 15 members, all from the Rajya Sabha
options.B: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.C: 22 members drawn from both Houses of Parliament
options.D: 45 members drawn from both Houses of Parliament

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Major Head 5002, Sub-Major Head 01 is used for capital which bears dividend liability.
2. Under the same Major Head, Sub-Major Head 02 is used for capital which is free of dividend liability.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: After rendering the March (Preliminary) Account Current, a zonal railway renders a second Account Current for March, styled the March (Final) Account Current. The main object of this second rendering is to:

options.A: Present the Budget Estimates of the following year to the Railway Board
options.B: Report the approximate earnings of the month of March
options.C: Obtain the supplementary grant for the month of March
options.D: Incorporate the adjustments and corrections received after the rendering of the March (Preliminary) account, so that the accounts of the financial year are closed completely and correctly

q: The earnings collected at a station of a zonal railway are required to be:

options.A: Utilised for meeting the contingent expenditure of the station
options.B: Retained at the station till the close of the financial year
options.C: Remitted in full to the Cash Office or the accredited bank, and not utilised for local expenditure
options.D: Adjusted against the imprest held by the Station Master

q: Under the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK), an assured annual outlay of Rs 20,000 crore is provided for safety-related works. The share of this annual outlay which the Railways meet from their own internal resources is:

options.A: Rs 10,000 crore
options.B: Rs 5,000 crore
options.C: Rs 15,000 crore
options.D: Rs 20,000 crore

q: The Financial Commissioner (Railways), who advises on all matters of railway finance at the apex level of the railway organisation, is:

options.A: A Member of the Railway Board and the principal financial adviser to the Board on matters of railway finance
options.B: The head of the Railway Audit organisation
options.C: The Chairman of the Indian Railway Finance Corporation
options.D: An officer of the Ministry of Finance deputed to conduct the audit of the railway accounts

q: Railway finances were separated from the general finances of the Government of India with effect from the year 1924-25, so that a separate Railway Budget came to be presented. This separation, under the Separation Convention, was given effect to through:

options.A: An Act of the British Parliament
options.B: The Government of India Act, 1935
options.C: A notification issued by the Railway Board
options.D: A resolution adopted by the Legislative Assembly

q: The main Demands for Grants presented with the Budget are examined by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees before the Lok Sabha votes on them. The Supplementary Demands for Grants presented during the course of the year differ in this respect, in that they are:

options.A: Examined by the Public Accounts Committee before they are voted
options.B: Voted only by the Rajya Sabha
options.C: Voted by the Lok Sabha without prior examination by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees
options.D: Presented only during the Budget session of Parliament

q: A probationer posted in the Budget section is asked to prepare a comparative note on two provisions of the Constitution relating to Union taxes and duties. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the duties referred to in Article 268 from the taxes referred to in Article 269?

options.A: The duties under Article 268 are levied and collected by the States themselves, whereas the taxes under Article 269 are shared between the Union and the States
options.B: The duties under Article 268 are levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States, whereas the taxes under Article 269 are levied and collected by the Union but assigned wholly to the States, their proceeds not forming part of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Both the duties under Article 268 and the taxes under Article 269 are levied, collected and retained by the Union alone
options.D: The duties under Article 268 are assigned to the States by the Finance Commission, whereas the taxes under Article 269 are levied by the States and collected by the Union

q: A dispute arises in the Finance Ministry over the final authority for deciding the net proceeds of a shareable Union tax for a year, the net proceeds being the gross proceeds reduced by the cost of collection. The amount is finally determined on the basis of:

options.A: The figures worked out by the Budget Division of the Ministry of Finance
options.B: The recommendations of the Finance Commission for that year
options.C: The calculation and certificate of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whose certificate is final
options.D: The report of the Public Accounts Committee on the Finance Accounts

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The salaries and allowances of the Judges of a High Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State concerned.
2. The pensions payable to or in respect of the Judges of a High Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A newly recruited Assistant has to brief his officer on the difference between the two Finance Commissions working in the federal structure of India. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the State Finance Commission from the Union Finance Commission?

options.A: Both the Commissions are constituted by the President under Article 280 of the Constitution
options.B: The State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor under Article 243-I of the Constitution to review the financial position of the Panchayats and the Municipalities, whereas the Union Finance Commission is constituted by the President under Article 280 to recommend the distribution of taxes between the Union and the States and the principles governing grants-in-aid
options.C: The State Finance Commission recommends the distribution of taxes between the Union and the States, whereas the Union Finance Commission reviews the finances of the Panchayats
options.D: The State Finance Commission is constituted by the President, whereas the Union Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor of each State in turn

q: A Member of Parliament, while going through the Budget papers, finds two explanatory documents with similar names and seeks to know how they differ from each other. The two documents are the 'Memorandum Explaining the Provisions in the Finance Bill' and the 'Notes on Demands for Grants'. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both the documents explain, clause by clause, the taxation proposals contained in the Finance Bill
options.B: The Memorandum explains, clause by clause, the provisions contained in the Finance Bill, whereas the Notes on Demands for Grants explain the nature, scope and reasons for the significant provisions made in the Demands for Grants
options.C: The Memorandum explains the provisions made in the Demands for Grants, whereas the Notes on Demands for Grants explain the provisions of the Finance Bill
options.D: The Memorandum is presented only to the Rajya Sabha, whereas the Notes on Demands for Grants are presented only to the Lok Sabha

q: In the Budget papers laid before Parliament, two documents relating to the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways bear similar titles, and a clerk is asked to bring out the difference between them. The two documents are the Detailed Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways and the 'Notes on Demands for Grants'. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: The Detailed Demands for Grants exhibit the estimates in detail, head-wise, with the figures of the actuals of the previous year and the Budget and Revised Estimates, whereas the Notes on Demands for Grants give brief explanatory notes on the nature, scope and reasons for the significant provisions made in the Demands
options.B: The Detailed Demands for Grants contain only explanatory notes, whereas the Notes on Demands for Grants exhibit the head-wise estimates
options.C: Both the documents contain the detailed classification of Major and Minor Heads of account prescribed in the Finance Code
options.D: The Detailed Demands for Grants are prepared by the zonal railways, whereas the Notes on Demands for Grants are prepared by the Audit Department

q: Two Parliamentary committees are sometimes confused with each other because both are concerned with the estimates and the accounts of the Ministries and the public undertakings. The two committees are the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: The Estimates Committee examines the estimates of the Ministries with a view to reporting what economies and improvements in organisation and efficiency can be effected consistent with the policy underlying the estimates, whereas the Committee on Public Undertakings examines the reports and accounts of the public undertakings to satisfy itself that their affairs are managed in accordance with sound business principles and prudent commercial practices
options.B: The Estimates Committee examines the accounts of the public undertakings, whereas the Committee on Public Undertakings examines the estimates of the Ministries
options.C: Both the Committees examine the Appropriation Accounts on the basis of the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General
options.D: The Estimates Committee consists of members of both Houses, whereas the Committee on Public Undertakings consists of members of the Lok Sabha alone

q: A probationer is asked to distinguish between the committee which examines the Demands for Grants before they are voted and the committee which examines the accounts after the expenditure has been incurred. The two committees are the Public Accounts Committee and the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both the Committees examine the Demands for Grants before they are voted by the Lok Sabha
options.B: The Public Accounts Committee examines, after the expenditure has been incurred, the Appropriation Accounts and the audit reports thereon, whereas the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways examines the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways before they are voted and presents a report which is recommendatory in character
options.C: The Public Accounts Committee votes the Demands for Grants after examination, whereas the Standing Committee regularises the excess expenditure of past years
options.D: The Public Accounts Committee is a committee of the Rajya Sabha alone, whereas the Standing Committee on Railways is a committee of the Lok Sabha alone

q: During the voting of the Demands for Grants, two kinds of cut motions with different objects are moved in the Lok Sabha, and a new member wants the distinction between them explained. The two motions are the 'policy cut' and the 'economy cut'. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both the motions propose that the Demand be reduced by a nominal sum of one hundred rupees
options.B: A policy cut proposes a reduction of the Demand by a specified amount, whereas an economy cut proposes that the Demand be reduced to one rupee
options.C: A policy cut proposes that the Demand be reduced to one rupee, in order to express disapproval of the policy underlying the Demand, whereas an economy cut proposes that the Demand be reduced by a specified amount, representing the economy that can be effected in the expenditure covered by the Demand
options.D: A policy cut can be moved only on a charged item, whereas an economy cut can be moved only in the Rajya Sabha

q: In the suspense and remittance section of the railway classification, two heads with similar names are operated in connection with the bank transactions of a railway. The two heads are 'Cheques and Bills' and 'Remittances into Banks'. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: 'Cheques and Bills' is operated for cheques and bills received and deposited with the bank, pending their realisation, and for cheques issued by the Railways, whereas 'Remittances into Banks' is operated for the earnings and other amounts remitted into the bank, pending credit by the bank
options.B: 'Cheques and Bills' is operated for the earnings remitted into the bank, whereas 'Remittances into Banks' is operated for the cheques deposited with the bank
options.C: Both the heads record the transactions of the Railways with the Pay and Accounts Offices of other Ministries
options.D: 'Cheques and Bills' represents amounts due from stations on traffic transactions, whereas 'Remittances into Banks' represents the deposits received from contractors

q: A survey is carried out for a proposed railway project, and a question arises how the preliminary expenses of the survey are to be treated in the two situations — where the project is later taken up for construction and where it is dropped. Which of the following correctly states the treatment of the preliminary expenses in the two situations?

options.A: Where the project surveyed is subsequently sanctioned and taken up for construction, the preliminary expenses form part of the capital cost of the work, whereas where the project is ultimately abandoned and not taken up, the preliminary expenses are charged to revenue as ordinary working expenses
options.B: In both the situations, the preliminary expenses are charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Where the project is taken up, the preliminary expenses are charged to revenue, whereas where it is abandoned, they are added to the capital cost of the work
options.D: In both the situations, the preliminary expenses are kept permanently under a suspense head

q: An audit party conducts two different kinds of audit on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, one relating to the availability of grants and the other to the canons of financial propriety. The two kinds are 'appropriation audit' and 'propriety audit'. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both the audits are concerned only with the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts
options.B: Appropriation audit examines expenditure against the canons of financial propriety, whereas propriety audit verifies the availability of grants
options.C: Appropriation audit is conducted by the Accounts Department as an internal check, whereas propriety audit is conducted by the Public Accounts Committee
options.D: Appropriation audit verifies that the moneys shown in the accounts as having been disbursed were legally available for, and were applied to, the services and purposes for which the grants and appropriations were made by Parliament, whereas propriety audit examines expenditure against the canons of financial propriety, bringing out cases of wasteful, infructuous or avoidable expenditure

q: Two systems of budgeting are referred to in a training lecture — one in which every item is justified afresh and the other in which outlays are related to physical results. The two systems are Zero-Based Budgeting and performance budgeting. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both the systems build the estimates of a year by adding a percentage increase to the expenditure of the previous year
options.B: Under Zero-Based Budgeting, every programme and item of expenditure is justified afresh from a zero base, without assuming that the existing level of expenditure will continue, whereas performance budgeting presents the estimates in terms of functions, programmes and activities, relating the financial outlays to the physical targets and results expected
options.C: Zero-Based Budgeting relates outlays to physical targets, whereas performance budgeting justifies every item afresh from a zero base
options.D: Zero-Based Budgeting is used only for the Capital Budget, whereas performance budgeting is used only for the Earnings Budget

q: A clerk confuses the last in-year review of the Budget, carried out in January, with the additional grant voted by Parliament during the year when the provision for a service proves insufficient. The two are the Final Modification Estimates and a Supplementary Grant. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: The Final Modification Estimates are the last review of the budget, carried out in January, in which the estimates are finally revised with reference to the actuals of the first nine months and the final requirements of the year, whereas a Supplementary Grant is an additional grant voted by Parliament during the year when the amount already granted for a service is found insufficient
options.B: The Final Modification Estimates are voted by Parliament as an additional grant, whereas a Supplementary Grant is an internal review carried out in January
options.C: Both the Final Modification Estimates and a Supplementary Grant are obtained after the close of the financial year
options.D: The Final Modification Estimates can be used to meet expenditure on a new service, whereas a Supplementary Grant cannot be so used

q: In financing the annual plan outlay of the Railways, two kinds of resources are referred to — those raised from the market and those generated by the Railways themselves. The two are Extra Budgetary Resources and the internal resources of the Railways. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both the resources are generated from the surplus of the Railways and carried in their fund balances
options.B: Extra Budgetary Resources are generated from the revenues of the Railways, whereas the internal resources are borrowed from the market
options.C: Extra Budgetary Resources are voted by Parliament as part of the Demands for Grants, whereas the internal resources require no budgetary provision at all
options.D: Extra Budgetary Resources are raised from the market, as through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation, and their servicing is the responsibility of the Railways, whereas the internal resources are generated by the Railways themselves from their revenues and fund balances and are used to finance a part of the plan outlay
